title: DFCN-CE3: A Three-Way Clustering Algorithm Based on Deep-Fusion Clustering Network
abstract: As an unsupervised learning method, deep clustering has received widespread attention and shown remarkable results for processing high-dimensional samples in the fields of data mining. However, most of the existing deep clustering algorithms define one cluster by a set with sharp boundary, which fails to capture the uncertainty and ambiguity prevalent in real-world datasets. To address this problem, this paper introduces a contraction-and-expansion based deep fusion three-way clustering network (DFCN-CE3 for short). The proposed method uses deep fusion clustering network to obtain hard clustering result of the universe. Base on the hard clustering result, DFCN-CE3 shrinks each cluster to the core region through a contraction operation, and enlarges each cluster to the support set through an expansion operation. By the contraction–expansion strategy, a three-way clustering result is formed. Comparisons of experimental results with 8 clustering algorithms on 6 data sets validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

evidence.title: DFCN-CE3: A Three-Way Clustering Algorithm Based on Deep-Fusion Clustering Network
evidence.abstract: As an unsupervised learning method, deep clustering has received widespread attention and shown remarkable results for processing high-dimensional samples in the fields of data mining. However, most of the existing deep clustering algorithms define one cluster by a set with sharp boundary, which fails to capture the uncertainty and ambiguity prevalent in real-world datasets. To address this problem, this paper introduces a contraction-and-expansion based deep fusion three-way clustering network (DFCN-CE3 for short). The proposed method uses deep fusion clustering network to obtain hard clustering result of the universe. Base on the hard clustering result, DFCN-CE3 shrinks each cluster to the core region through a contraction operation, and enlarges each cluster to the support set through an expansion operation. By the contraction–expansion strategy, a three-way clustering result is formed. Comparisons of experimental results with 8 clustering algorithms on 6 data sets validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Beyond Surface Metrics: Modeling Abstractivity in Summarization via Action-Based Spectrums
abstract: Traditional views of abstractive summarization treat it as a free-form rephrasing of the source text, yet this notion is vague and difficult to measure; existing evaluations rely on surface-level metrics — such as novel n-gram counts, extractive fragment coverage, or extractive fragment density — that obscure the stylistic nuances that distinguish summaries along an abstractivity spectrum. We therefore propose a fine-grained, continuous characterization that unifies extractive and abstractive summarization as two endpoints of a single spectrum defined by the frequency of text-transformation actions (sentence reduction, combination, paraphrasing, reordering, etc.) drawn from the foundational summarization literature. To operationalize this view, we introduce CLAsum, a human-annotated dataset comprising 600 unique samples; these arise from 200 document–summary pairs sourced from CNN/DailyMail and XSum datasets, each annotated by three independent annotators who assign one of five perceived abstractivity levels and record the prevalence of seven abstractivity-inducing actions per pair. Our analysis demonstrates a strong correlation between these action frequencies and human judgments, validating the spectrum, while automatic prediction of the resulting Abstractivity-Inducing Features (AIFs) captures signals that existing metrics miss and yields significant gains in abstractivity-level measuremnt. This work delivers both conceptual clarity and practical tools for building controllable, style-aware summarization systems capable of producing summaries with precisely specified levels of abstractivity, thereby advancing the field toward truly user-tailored, task-adaptive summarization.

title: SHIFT: Self-Healing Intelligence in Feature Store and Data Store Transitions
abstract: This study presents an AI model management method for maintaining the predictive performance of virtual metrology (VM) systems in steel manufacturing processes. The proposed method addresses concept drift (CD), a major threat to long-term model reliability, by orchestrating a dual-update strategy that autonomously revises both the feature store and the data store. Unlike conventional model maintenance approaches based on static inputs and accumulated data, our framework continuously reassesses feature relevance and adapts retraining datasets to reflect evolving process conditions. Applied to a real-world steel sintering process, the method achieved significant recovery in predictive accuracy—from a post-deployment drop of 65% to over 93% after updates. This study highlights the importance of proactive maintenance for AI models and demonstrates how an intelligent update strategy can extend the usable life and reliability of VM systems in critical production workflows. The findings contribute to the broader field of AI-enabled asset management by offering a scalable solution for condition monitoring, retraining scheduling, and long-term performance assurance.

title: Distilling knowledge from AI models used to detect heart conditions in 12-lead ECG traces
abstract: Abstract Background/Introduction Deep learning matches or exceeds expert arrhythmia detection, but its black-box nature limits clinical use. Explainable AI (XAI) can accelerate cardiovascular research by converting accurate AI predictions into actionable human knowledge, especially in underexplored domains. However, ECG-focused XAI faces issues: analyses limited to single predictions, superficial heatmaps lacking causal depth, and vulnerability to cherry-picking. Concept Relevance Propagation (CRP) offers dataset-wide, concept-level explanations, but has not been adopted for ECG data in cardiovascular applications and lacks thorough medical data validation. Purpose In this work, we tested the hypothesis that CRP can translate AI insights into human-understandable knowledge in a quantitatively and qualitatively verifiable way. To evaluate this, we analyzed a high-performing model predicting atrial fibrillation (AF) and assessed how its patterns align with clinical knowledge. Methods To enable our analysis, we adapted a state of the art ECG model in PyTorch via knowledge distillation, training on PTB-XL (median age 62, IQR 22, 52% male) and validating on CPSC-2018 (median age 62, IQR 26, 54% male) using AUROC. A custom canonizer/composite enabled CRP through batch-norm-rich residual blocks. We validated implementation choices using Symmetric Relevance Gain (SRG) bit-flipping across layers. Concepts were ranked by mean relevance for AF prediction across both datasets and visualized with RelMax. To test faithfulness, we pruned the model to the top <0.5% most relevant nodes in the final layer and re-evaluated performance. Qualitative interpretation of selected concepts was done with a clinical expert. Results Our distilled model reached an AUROC of 0.96 for AF, with pruning to <0.5% of the most relevant last-layer nodes with similar AUROC (+0.01), suggesting good out of distribution performance using just 25 nodes. Concept analysis showed that higher-level concepts focused on consistent ECG regions, while lower-layer ones aligned with specific wave components. Expert adjudication found that, although classification logic was interpretable for single ECGs, the CRP-enabled global analysis revealed that intermediate nodes often combine multiple medical concepts, limiting interpretability (Figure). Conclusion This is the first quantitative application of CRP to ECG and arrhythmia analysis. Our open-source pipeline integrates state-of-the-art XAI methods. While CRP enables more quantitative and causal reasoning about model decisions, our findings also expose current limitations. A key challenge ahead is improving concept purity, potentially by incorporating it directly into model training.Relevance Heatmap of Concept 9 for AFRelevance Heatmap of Concept 93 for AF

title: SSCBKA-optimized machine learning for hyperspectral classification of maize seeds for agricultural quality control
abstract: The high latitude of hyperspectral data poses significant difficulties for data processing. Machine learning has demonstrated unique advantages in handling high-latitude data. However, traditional machine learning is limited in model performance due to unreasonable setting of internal parameter values. Therefore, this paper proposes the use of an improved Black-winged Kite algorithm to optimize the parameters of a machine learning algorithm for processing hyperspectral data. First, maize seeds were collected from the test site, and hyperspectral data of the maize seeds were obtained using hyperspectral instruments. Secondly, to enhance the global search ability of the Black-winged kite algorithm, this paper proposes a new improved mechanism called nonlinear time-varying perturbation sine and cosine strategy, which incorporates this strategy into the migration behavior of the black-winged kite algorithm. At the same time, to enhance the population diversity of the black-winged kite algorithm, the vertical and horizontal crossover strategy is introduced into the position update of the algorithm. Again, to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, the proposed algorithm was compared with seven meta-heuristic optimization algorithms and ten newer meta-heuristic optimization algorithm variants in dimensions of 10, 30, 50, and 100 based on the CEC2017 test function. Finally, the improved algorithm was applied to hyperparameter optimize the extreme random tree and random forest respectively and compared with the other nine models based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Scorse. Experimental results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper converges the fastest and optimizes the best compared with other algorithms. The accuracy of the improved extreme random tree has been 88.268%, the precision has been 94.805%, the recall has been 81.100%, and the F1-Scorse has been 87.425%. The improved random forest achieved 89.385% accuracy, 88.172% precision, 91.100% recall, and 89.617% F1-Scorse.
